evals.prompt: Create docs for one API set: GET /users is implemented, POST /users is proposed, and DELETE /users/{id} conflicts between requirements and source.
evals.expected_output: A coordinated API package with authority and status per operation.
expectations: Does not choose one global mode.
Marks GET implemented, POST proposed, and DELETE conflicting with evidence.
Produces one repository-native or requested primary artifact by default.
Keeps evidence analysis and conflict details out of settled endpoint reference sections.

evals.prompt: Review the API documentation for integration defects. Do not rewrite or edit files.
evals.expected_output: Findings, Open Questions, and recommendations only.
expectations: Leads with actionable findings.
Does not output rewritten artifacts.
Does not write files.
forbidden_behaviors: Rewrites the contract
Edits documentation files

evals.prompt: Create this REST contract as OpenAPI YAML only; do not add Markdown.
expectations: Honors the explicit single-format request.
Does not add Markdown integration documentation.

evals.prompt: Reconcile frontend and backend API evidence; do not perform a full rewrite.
evals.expected_output: A difference list and only defensible fragments.
expectations: Lists differences and owners.
Does not silently choose a side.
Does not perform a complete rewrite without authorization.

evals.prompt: Document the provider-initiated HTTP payment webhook.
evals.expected_output: An OpenAPI webhook contract with evidenced delivery behavior.
expectations: Uses top-level webhooks where supported.
Does not model the webhook as a callback or message channel.

evals.prompt: Document the callback URL supplied in POST /exports and invoked when processing completes.
expectations: Uses callbacks bound to the initiating operation.
Does not model it as a provider-configured webhook.

evals.prompt: Document the Kafka order.created topic and consumer acknowledgement behavior.
expectations: Uses AsyncAPI channel and message semantics.
Does not force the message into an OpenAPI path.

evals.prompt: The frontend was built first from the supplied types and client calls. Write concise Markdown API documentation for the backend team to implement. Do not include an analysis report.
evals.expected_output: A compact backend implementation contract grouped by endpoint.
expectations: Documents method, path, request fields, success response, and relevant errors from the frontend evidence.
Uses one Markdown deliverable because the prompt requests Markdown.
Keeps unresolved implementation decisions as local TBD items only when they block the contract.
Does not include source inventory, evidence matrix, frontend implementation notes, risk register, recommendations, or conclusion.
forbidden_behaviors: Adds a source analysis section
Adds an evidence or status legend
Adds implementation recommendations unrelated to the contract
Creates an additional OpenAPI artifact

evals.prompt: Generate the existing user endpoint documentation for frontend integration. Follow the repository's OpenAPI format and do not add a separate Markdown guide.
evals.expected_output: A concise OpenAPI contract matching the backend behavior.
expectations: Documents the implemented method, path, authentication, parameters, response schema, and evidenced errors.
Uses short operation summaries and field-level constraints.
Produces OpenAPI only and does not duplicate the contract in Markdown.
Does not expose source file paths or narrate the inspection process.
forbidden_behaviors: Creates a Markdown companion document
Includes a codebase evidence report
Invents undocumented response fields or errors
Marks response properties as required from the single response example
Adds uuid or date-time formats to response fields based on their names or example values
Copies the path parameter UUID constraint onto the response id field
Invents an API version such as 1.0.0

evals.prompt: Generate an OpenAPI 3.1 YAML contract for frontend integration from the supplied backend evidence. Keep observed examples, but include only schema guarantees that the evidence actually proves.
evals.expected_output: A machine-readable draft whose constraints remain within the exact evidence boundary.
expectations: Documents the required accountId path parameter and its evidenced pattern.
Documents the evidenced accounts:read security scope.
Keeps captured payloads as examples without promoting their observed values to universal constraints.
Either obtains an API version before finalizing or represents the unevidenced required metadata as an explicit draft TBD.
forbidden_behaviors: Adds required arrays to response or error schemas without presence evidence
Marks nickname nullable solely because one captured value is null
Defines state as an enum or const from the value active
Adds uuid, date-time, email, URI, or another format based on field names or examples
Transfers the accountId pattern to response id
States that undocumented rate limits, caching, retries, or errors do not exist
Silently sets info.version to 1.0.0
Emits an OAuth2 security scheme with empty flows
Emits a malformed security requirement object or invents a scope mapping
Leaves unresolved references or examples that fail the declared specification validator

evals.prompt: Rewrite the supplied API notes as a standard concise API reference. Keep only what a frontend engineer needs to call the API.
evals.expected_output: A lookup-oriented API reference without report-style padding.
expectations: Uses shared authentication and error rules once instead of repeating them per endpoint.
Includes only applicable endpoint sections and representative examples.
Omits empty sections and generic HTTP explanations.
Does not add table of contents, architecture narrative, status legend, risk register, recommendations, changelog, or conclusion.
forbidden_behaviors: Explains basic REST or HTTP concepts
Repeats the same shared rule under every endpoint
Adds non-blocking open questions
Adds a document-generation summary inside the reference
